You have been careful to leave the door of the cage open over night, and have put some maize inside the cage. A strong cord attached to the door is passed across the doorway and round a wooden "runner" on the opposite post, and then to the back of the cage, where your man lies concealed.

arxiv-2109-13177.title: Robust Equilibria in General Competing Mechanism Games Thanks: First version: April 13, 2021
arxiv-2109-13177.creator: Seungjin Han
arxiv-2109-13177.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Seungjin Han. This paper proposes the notion of robust PBE in a general competing mechanism game of incomplete information where a mechanism allows its designer to send a message to himself at the same time agents send messages. It identifies the utility environments where the notion of robust PBE coincides with that of strongly robust PBE (Epstein and Peters (1999), Han (2007)) and with that of robust PBE respectively.

arxiv-2202-12952.title: Superconductivity in cuprates governed by topological constraints
arxiv-2202-12952.creator: Yves Noat, Alain Mauger, William Sacks
arxiv-2202-12952.description: Abstract Résumé The remarkable universality of the cuprate T c T_{c} dome suggests a very fundamental unifying principle. Moreover, the superconducting gap is known to persist above T c T_{c} in the pseudogap phase of all cuprates. So, contrary to BCS, the gap cannot be the order parameter of the transition.

arxiv-2303-08209.title: Learning to Adapt the Parameters of Behavior Trees and Motion Generators (BTMGs) to Task Variations
arxiv-2303-08209.creator: Faseeh Ahmad, Matthias Mayr, Volker Krueger
arxiv-2303-08209.description: Abstract The ability to learn new tasks and quickly adapt to different variations or dimensions is an important attribute in agile robotics. In our previous work, we have explored Behavior Trees and Motion Generators (BTMGs) as a robot arm policy representation to facilitate the learning and execution of assembly tasks.

arxiv-2405-01562.title: Discrete Event Simulation: It’s Easy with SimPy!
arxiv-2405-01562.creator: Dmitry Zinoviev
arxiv-2405-01562.description: Abstract . This paper introduces the practicalities and benefits of using SimPy, a discrete event simulation (DES) module written in Python, for modeling and simulating complex systems. Through a step-by-step exploration of the classical Dining Philosophers Problem, we demonstrate how SimPy enables the efficient construction of discrete event models, emphasizing system states, transitions, and event handling.

arxiv-2409-07249.title: The H ∞ H^{\infty} -functional calculus for bisectorial Clifford operators
arxiv-2409-07249.creator: F. Mantovani, P. Schlosser
arxiv-2409-07249.description: Abstract . The aim of this article is to introduce the H ∞ H^{\infty} -functional calculus for unbounded bisectorial operators in a Clifford module over the algebra ℝ n \mathbb{R}_{n} . This work is based on the universality property of the S S -functional calculus, which shows its applicability to fully Clifford operators.

arxiv-2411-01943.title: Brainbots as smart autonomous active particles with programmable motion Preprint: DRAFT v1.6 - August 7, 2026
arxiv-2411-01943.creator: M. Noirhomme, I. Mammadli, N. Vanesse, J. Pande, A.-S. Smith, N. Vandewalle
arxiv-2411-01943.description: Abstract We present an innovative robotic device designed to provide controlled motion for studying active matter. Motion is driven by an internal vibrator powered by a small rechargeable battery. The system integrates acoustic and magnetic sensors along with a programmable microcontroller. Unlike conventional vibrobots, the motor induces horizontal vibrations, resulting in cycloidal trajectories that have been characterized and optimized.

arxiv-2412-12386.title: Interpretable LLM-based Table Question Answering
arxiv-2412-12386.creator: Giang Nguyen nguyengiangbkhn@gmail.com, Ivan Brugere ivan.brugere@jpmchase.com, Shubham Sharma shubham.x2.sharma@jpmchase.com, Sanjay Kariyappa skariyappa@nvidia.com, Anh Totti Nguyen anh.ng8@gmail.com, Freddy Lecue lecue.freddy@gmail.com
arxiv-2412-12386.description: Abstract Interpretability in Table Question Answering (Table QA) is critical, especially in high-stakes domains like finance and healthcare. While recent Table QA approaches based on Large Language Models (LLMs) achieve high accuracy, they often produce ambiguous explanations of how answers are derived. We propose Plan-of-SQLs ( POS ), a new Table QA method that makes the model’s decision-making process interpretable.

arxiv-2504-13239.title: The first-order orbital equation
arxiv-2504-13239.creator: Maurizio M. D’Eliseo a
arxiv-2504-13239.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Maurizio M. D’Eliseo a. We derive the first-order orbital equation employing a complex variable formalism. We then examine Newton’s theorem on precessing orbits and apply it to the perihelion shift of an elliptic orbit in general relativity. It is found that corrections to the inverse-square gravitational force law formally similar to that required by general relativity were suggested by Clairaut in the 18th century.

arxiv-2505-15016.title: Two-Terminal Electrical Detection of the Néel Vector via Longitudinal Antiferromagnetic Nonreciprocal Transport
arxiv-2505-15016.creator: Guozhi Long, Hui Zeng, Mingxiang Pan, Wenhui Duan, Huaqing Huang
arxiv-2505-15016.description: Abstract We propose a robust two-terminal electrical readout scheme for detecting the Néel vector orientation in antiferromagnetic (AFM) materials by leveraging longitudinal nonreciprocal transport driven by quantum metric dipoles. Unlike conventional readout mechanisms, our approach does not require spin-polarized electrodes, tunneling junctions, or multi-terminal geometries, offering a universal and scalable solution for AFM spintronics.

arxiv-2507-19876.title: A unified diagrammatic formulation of single-reference and multi-reference random phase approximations: the particle-hole and particle-particle channels
arxiv-2507-19876.creator: Yuqi Wang, Wei-Hai Fang, Zhendong Li
arxiv-2507-19876.description: Abstract A diagrammatic multi-reference generalization of many-body perturbation theory was recently introduced [J. Phys. Chem. Lett., 2025, 16, 3047]. This framework allows us to extend single-reference (SR) Green’s function methods defined at the diagrammatic level naturally into multi-reference case, as previously exemplified by the formulation of multi-reference direct random phase approximation (MR-dRPA) and the multi-reference second-order screened exchange approximation (MR-SOSEX).

arxiv-2509-22986.title: CryptoSRAM: Enabling High-Throughput Cryptography on MCUs via In-SRAM Computing
arxiv-2509-22986.creator: Jingyao Zhang, Elaheh Sadredini
arxiv-2509-22986.description: Abstract Secure communication is a critical requirement for Internet of Things (IoT) devices, which are often based on Microcontroller Units (MCUs). Current cryptographic solutions, which rely on software libraries or dedicated hardware accelerators, are fundamentally limited by the performance and energy costs of data movement between memory and processing units.

This study aimed to clarify the prevalence, associated factors, and the magnitude of association with mortality and incident disability for sarcopenia and combinations of its components among Japanese commu

plos-pone-0010631.creator: Hong Shang, Ping Zhong, Jing Liu et al.
plos-pone-0010631.description: PLOS ONE research article. Co-infection with HIV-1 and HCV is a significant global public health problem and a major consideration for anti-HIV-1 treatment. HCV infection among HIV-1 positive people who are eligible for the newly launched nationwide anti-HIV-1 treatment program in China has not been well c

pmc-10653643.title: A novel N-heterocycles substituted oseltamivir derivatives as potent inhibitors of influenza virus neuraminidase: discovery, synthesis and biological evaluation
pmc-10653643.creator: Jiwei Zhang, Chuanfeng Liu, Ruifang Jia, Xujie Zhang, Jian Zhang, Chiara Bertagnin, Anna Bonomini, Laura Guizzo, Yuanmin Jiang, Huinan Jia, Shuzhen Jia, Xiuli Ma, Arianna Loregian, Bing Huang, Peng Zhan, Xinyong Liu
pmc-10653643.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Our previous studies have shown that the introduction of structurally diverse benzyl side chains at the C5-NH2 position of oseltamivir to occupy 150-cavity contributes to the binding affinity with neuraminidase and anti-influenza activity. To obtain broad-spectrum neuraminidase inhibitors, we designed and synthesised a series of novel oseltamivir derivatives bearing different N-heterocycles substituents that have been proved to induce opening of the 150-loop of group-2 neuraminidases.

pmc-10711417.title: Investigating the Impact of Irrigation on Malaria Vector Larval Habitats and Transmission Using a Hydrology‐Based Model
pmc-10711417.creator: Ai‐Ling Jiang, Ming‐Chieh Lee, Prashanth Selvaraj, Teshome Degefa, Hallelujah Getachew, Hailu Merga, Delenasaw Yewhalaw, Guiyun Yan, Kuolin Hsu
pmc-10711417.description: A combination of accelerated population growth and severe droughts has created pressure on food security and driven the development of irrigation schemes across sub‐Saharan Africa. Irrigation has been associated with increased malaria risk, but risk prediction remains difficult due to the heterogeneity of irrigation and the environment.

pmc-10738188.title: DEPRESSION AND LONELINESS IN BLACK WOMEN WITH HYPERTENSION: A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
pmc-10738188.creator: Lashawn Hutto, Michelle Odlum, Maritza Dowling, Laurie Theeke
pmc-10738188.description: Hypertension occurs more frequently in Black women than men. Over 50% of Black women have hypertension, compared to 39% of non-Hispanic white women and 38% of Hispanic women. Black women with hypertension are more likely to report depressive symptoms which are associated with hypertension, a known risk for cardiovascular diseases including myocardial infarction, heart failure, and stroke.

pmc-11738178.title: Weight Management Quality Improvement Project in Tower Hamlets Community Learning Disability Service
pmc-11738178.creator: Lucy Dundas, Irem Deniz, Genevieve Hirsz, David Prior, Nicole Eady
pmc-11738178.description: AimsThe project's aim is to record up-to-date BMI readings of 70% or more of our service users by September 2024. We have identified barriers limiting current data collection, such as challenges weighing wheelchair bound clients or limited availability of weighing scales, and will action our change idea methods to reach our target in this time period.

pmc-12447398.title: Large-scale Investigations of Water Diffusion in Metal–Organic Frameworks with One-Dimensional Channels
pmc-12447398.creator: I-Ting Sung, Li-Chiang Lin
pmc-12447398.description: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), known for their highly versatile nature, show considerable promise as adsorbents and membranes for water-related applications such as water harvesting and water filtration. One of the key factors that may influence their efficiency is the diffusion of water within MOFs. However, the behaviors and mechanisms of water diffusion in MOFs remain relatively underexplored.

pmc-12553594.title: Impact of RSV hospitalization on healthcare costs, caregivers’ productivity loss, and quality of life in children ≤ 2 years old in five European countries
pmc-12553594.creator: Joanne G Wildenbeest, Louis Bont, Daniela Cianci, Geert W J Frederix, Cristina Calvo, Johannes Liese, Renato Cutrera, Chiara Azzari, Jacques Brouard, Federico Martinon-Torres, Egbert Herting, Simon B Drysdale, Ralph Epaud, Atul Gupta, Madelyn Ruggieri, Yoonyoung Choi, BRICE Study Group
pmc-12553594.description: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of hospitalizations in young children globally. We evaluated direct medical costs, caregiver work loss, and child quality of life (QoL) impairment associated with RSV hospitalization. Children ≤ 2 years with laboratory-confirmed RSV infection were prospectively identified between October 2020 and May 2023 at ten hospitals in Germany, Spain, Italy, France, and England.

pmc-12736144.title: How the Intake of Pulses May Impact Metabolic Disorders and Dementia Risk: A Narrative Review
pmc-12736144.creator: Lisa M B Salinas, Maricarmen Marroquin, Mariana Mendez, Isabel Omaña-Guzmán, Juan C Lopez-Alvarenga, Christopher Papandreou
pmc-12736144.description: We present a narrative review focusing on pulses’ geographical origin and distribution, their impact on human evolution and history, and their influence on human health. Pulses, including dry peas, beans, and lentils, are renowned for their richness in chemical antioxidants. Despite containing antinutrients, processing techniques preserve their health advantages.

pmc-13006411.title: Instant messaging-based digital health interventions for diabetes management: a domain-structured systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-13006411.creator: Shan Chen, Emma Mirza Wati Mohamad, Arina Anis Azlan, Xixi Zhao
pmc-13006411.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundInstant messaging delivered through social platforms is increasingly used to support diabetes self-management. However, evidence remains difficult to interpret because trials vary widely in platform choice, intervention design, outcome constructs, and measurement instruments.ObjectiveTo synthesize the effects of instant-messaging interventions for diabetes across pre-specified outcome domains, and to explore whether platform type, follow-up duration, and study size help explain variation in effect estimates.MethodsWe searched seven databases (2010–2025) for randomized controlled trials in which diabetes interventions were primarily delivered via instant-messaging/social platforms.

pmc-13336112.title: SSR4 Sustains Tertiary Lymphoid Structures by Regulation Quality Control of N‐linked Glycosylation During B‐cell Differentiation Into Plasmacyte in Colorectal Cancer
pmc-13336112.creator: Wei Zhao, Youcai Zhao, Haiyang Li, Bowen Yang, Siyan Lu, Xueting Fu, Caixia Zhang, Yirong Chen, Xiaofeng Bian, Xinghua Ma, Xiaobing Yang, Bin Wang, Yuan Fang, Lulu Yang, Yelin Zhao, Shuli Zhao
pmc-13336112.description: Intratumoral tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) fosters B‐cell differentiation and antibody production, yet the intrinsic programs sustaining these functions remain unclear. By integrating spatial transcriptomics and single‐cell RNA sequencing of colorectal cancer, we delineate a B‐cell trajectory enriched for endoplasmic reticulum protein processing, autophagy, NF‐κB signaling, and N‐linked glycosylation, highlighting SSR4 as a progressively induced TRAP‐complex component.

pmc-13376174.title: Jets from a stellar-mass black hole are as relativistic as those from supermassive black holes
pmc-13376174.creator: X Zhang, W Yu, F Carotenuto, R Fender, S Motta, A Bahramian, J C A Miller-Jones, T D Russell, S Corbel, P A Woudt, P Atri, C Knigge, G R Sivakoff, A K Hughes, J van den Eijnden, J H Matthews, M C Baglio, P Saikia
pmc-13376174.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Relativistic jets from supermassive black holes in active galactic nuclei are amongst the most powerful phenomena in the universe. Similar jets from stellar-mass black holes offer a chance to study the phenomena on accessible observation time scales. However, such comparative studies across black hole masses and time scales remain hampered by the long-standing perception that stellar-mass black hole jets are in a less relativistic regime.

pmc-13553083.title: Life after loss: gendered changes in social networks and community participation around widowhood
pmc-13553083.creator: Elisa Tambellini, Mirkka Danielsbacka, Antti O Tanskanen, Anna Rotkirch, Nekehia T Quashie
pmc-13553083.description: ObjectivesThis study examined how widowhood shapes older adults’ close network composition and quality and community participation, and whether these effects differ by gender.MethodsData from the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE) were used to analyze 55,555 Europeans aged 50 and older, including 3,257 who became widowed between survey waves.

pmc-13579656.title: Effects and Moderators of Exergaming on Glucose and Lipid Metabolism in Children and Adolescents: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-13579656.creator: Shuo Zhou, Yang Yang, Xiaoquan Weng, Huakun Zheng, Lingyan Yuan, Stefano Brini
pmc-13579656.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundExergaming, or active video gaming, may make physical activity more engaging for children and adolescents. Earlier reviews have focused on activity, adiposity, fitness, or psychosocial outcomes, leaving effects on glycemic and lipid biomarkers uncertain.

pmc-13675781.title: Could calcitonin gene‐related peptide inhibitors prevent status epilepticus?
pmc-13675781.creator: Michael Nsaka, Noor Baban, Sepideh Allahdadian, Armin Scheffler, Diana Lindner, Dagny Holle, Alain Lekoubou
pmc-13675781.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Calcitonin gene‐related peptide (CGRP) inhibitors modulate pain and neuroinflammation, a recognized contributor to epileptogenesis and status epilepticus (SE). We examined the association between CGRP inhibitor use and SE hospitalization in epilepsy patients with comorbid migraine. Using TriNetX (130 healthcare organizations), we identified patients with epilepsy from May 2018 through May 2026, and propensity‐matched cohorts for age, sex, race, anti‐seizure medications (ASMs), migraine diagnosis, migraine treatments, and cognitive impairment. The primary outcome was SE occurrence.
